name: build-me-an-agent
query: Build me an agent that watches our contracts folder and summarizes anything new that lands in it.
why: The core build request. Intake runs first, the stack is committed slot by slot, and the run may rightly conclude that a scheduled script beats an agent.

name: add-an-ai-feature-to-an-existing-app
query: Add an AI feature to our Rails app that suggests tags for each post as the author writes it.
why: Adding an AI subsystem to an existing repo is explicitly this skill's, not ai-engineering's. The existing footprint becomes an intake constraint rather than a reason to skip intake.

name: scaffold-a-project
query: Scaffold an agent project for a local-first coding assistant that runs against Ollama.
why: Direct scaffold request with two intake fields already answered. The rest still get gathered, and the exit contract holds every slot to a named component or a justified not needed.

name: stack-for-a-committed-build
query: We've committed to building a document-extraction service this quarter. Which stack should we use?
why: The hardest positive. It is phrased as a stack question, which reads like ai-engineering, but a specific system is being built, so it needs intake and a committed stack rather than a survey of options.

name: vague-ai-idea
query: I want to build something with AI for our sales team. Not sure what yet.
why: Too vague to answer the intake fields, so this skill calls interview-me and idea-refine to get the idea into focus, then carries it into a stack.

name: agent-where-a-script-would-do
query: Build me an agent that renames files in this folder to match our naming convention.
why: Fires precisely so the premise gets challenged. Every build-me-an-agent request comes here, and the intake concluding no agent is needed is a correct outcome, not a miss.

name: options-with-no-build
query: What are my options for a vector store if we're OSS-only?
why: Belongs to ai-engineering, which owns open-ended options questions. No system is named and nothing is being built, so there is nothing to run intake on.

name: orienting-on-a-layer
query: What's the current state of agent memory frameworks? Just orienting, nothing to build yet.
why: Belongs to ai-engineering. Build intent is explicitly disclaimed, which is the discriminator on this seam.

name: write-an-mcp-server
query: Write an MCP server that exposes our internal ticketing API.
why: Belongs to build-mcp-server. This skill names which MCP servers a stack needs; building one is never hand-rolled here.

name: log-a-tool-failure
query: Log that the framework we picked last month broke on install under the new Python.
why: Belongs to ai-engineering-update, which owns field notes. A component that fights back during a build produces a note there, not a new scaffold run.

name: scaffold-a-plain-web-app
query: Scaffold a new Next.js dashboard for our internal metrics.
why: General application work with no AI subsystem, so it routes to agent-skills. Guards against firing on the word scaffold alone.

name: fix-the-scaffolded-code
query: The agent loop we scaffolded last week crashes when a tool returns null. Fix it.
why: Implementation and debugging belong to agent-skills. Scaffolding is the starting line; this skill does not reimplement build, test or review.

name: research-before-choosing
query: Research which agent frameworks support streaming tool calls, with sources and dates.
why: Belongs to deep-research. A verified-facts request with no system to build and no stack to commit.
